plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and rose-like flowers. It thrives in mild, humid climates and is a mainstay of winter gardens in warm temperate regions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (December to April in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and China; widely cultivated in the southeastern United States, Western Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, a close relative, is the plant that produces all true tea, including green, black, and oolong.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: A small bulbous perennial with drooping, bell-shaped white flowers marked with green on the inner petals. It often pushes up through snow and frost, heralding the end of winter.
plants.location: Native to Europe from the Pyrenees to Ukraine; naturalized in the UK, North America, and elsewhere
plants.funFact: Snowdrops produce galantamine, a compound used in medication to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that produces fragrant blossoms on bare branches in the depths of winter. It is highly valued in East Asian culture and often blooms before the leaves emerge.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: Native to southern China; cultivated across China, Japan, Korea, and Vietnam
plants.funFact: In Chinese culture, plum blossom is one of the 'Three Friends of Winter' along with pine and bamboo, symbolizing perseverance and resilience.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A spreading tropical tree with fern-like leaves and a canopy covered in brilliant clusters of flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere summer it is in full display, followed by long woody seed pods.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere (December to February) and in the dry season in some tropical regions
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; widely planted in tropical and subtropical regions, including northern Australia, Brazil, and southern Africa
plants.funFact: Despite its global popularity, the flamboyant tree is endangered in its native Madagascar because of habitat loss.
